verdict.rationale: The only first-party evidence is the Obsidian Sync headless client. It syncs vaults without the desktop app and is described as useful for CI pipelines, agents and automated workflows, so it is an official, non-GUI tool aimed at agent use. Its scope is limited to syncing, and the evidence never describes it as a general CLI with note or vault commands. Obsidian URI and plain-text file access are adjacent mechanisms and earn no credit. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an official CLI with commands beyond sync (read, create, search or edit notes), CLI usage and reference docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Obsidian Sync offers a headless client to sync vaults without using the desktop app. Useful for CI pipelines, agents, and automated workflows.
